newsitem.title: USA: FERC approves El Paso gas line expansion.
newsitem.headline: FERC approves El Paso gas line expansion.

text.p: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) approved El Paso Natural Gas Co's $19.5 million gas pipeline expansion project in Arizona, the Texas-based company said.

The pipeline company plans to expand capacity by 180 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of the Havasu Crossover line between El Paso's north and south systems in Mojave and La Paz counties of Arizona.
The new capacity will enable shippers to tap into the plentiful reserves in the San Juan, Anadarko and Permian Basins, as well as off the east end of the system.

The expansion, expected to take about five months, involves installing a 14,000 horsepower turbine compressor at El Paso's Alamo Lake compressor station and improvements to existing compressors at Alamo Lake, Dutch Flat, and Wenden.
El Paso will also perform piping modifications at Franconia Junction and Wenden compressor station and install cooling units at Alamo Lake and Wenden.
El Paso Natural Gas, a unit of El Paso Energy Corp, filed the expansion application with FERC on April 15.
